'''Robert Arnold Alberty''' (1921–2014) was an American [[biophysical chemistry|biophysical chemist]], professor emeritus at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], and a member of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]].

Alberty earned bachelor's and master's degrees from the [[University of Nebraska–Lincoln|University of Nebraska]] in 1943 and 1944, respectively, then a doctoral degree from the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] in 1947. For his work in the area of [[biochemical thermodynamics]], Alberty was elected to the National Academy of Sciences in 1965. In 1968 he was elected a Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref name=AAAS>{{cite web|title=Book of Members, 1780-2010: Chapter A|url=http://www.amacad.org/publications/BookofMembers/ChapterA.pdf|publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences|accessdate=6 April 2011}}</ref> He was dean of the MIT School of Science between 1967-1982.

Alberty is also known for his textbooks on [[physical chemistry]], which have gone through many editions. The first one, ''Physical Chemistry'', co-authored with [[Farrington Daniels]], was published in 1957. More recent books of the same title have been co-authored with [[Robert J. Silbey]] and [[Moungi G. Bawendi]] (2004). Other works include ''Thermodynamics of Biochemical Reactions  '' (2003) and ''Biochemical Thermodynamics: Applications of Mathematica (Methods of Biochemical Analysis)'' (2006).

He died in Cambridge, Massachusetts, at the age of 92 on January 18, 2014.<ref>[http://web.mit.edu/newsoffice/2014/robert-alberty-professor-emeritus-of-chemistry-and-former-dean-of-science-dies-at-92.html Robert Alberty, professor emeritus of chemistry and former dean of science, dies at 92]</ref> Towards the end of his life he wrote a short account of his life and scientific career.<ref name = "autob">{{cite journal | doi= 10.1021/jp103554e| title= Brief Scientific Autobiography of Robert A. Alberty| year= 2010| last1= Alberty| first1= Robert A.| journal= The Journal of Physical Chemistry B| volume= 114| issue= 49| pages= 16047–16050| pmid= 21141926}}</ref>

==Research==

At the beginning of his career Alberty worked principally on aspects of [[electrophoresis]] in [[protein chemistry]].<ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1021/j150457a018| title= Homogenicity and the Electrophoretic Behavior of Some Proteins| year= 1948| last1= Alberty| first1= Robert A.| last2= Anderson| first2= Elmer A.| last3= Williams| first3= J. W.| journal= The Journal of Physical and Colloid Chemistry| volume= 52| issue= 1| pages= 217–230| pmid= 18918870}}</ref> After a period of 20 years away from academic research, when he had administrative responsibilities at MIT, together with work in the petroleum industry,<ref name = "autob"/> he returned to biochemical research.

He became increasingly concerned with the [[enzyme kinetics|kinetics]] and [[enzyme mechanisms|mechanisms]] of [[Enzyme catalysis|enzyme-catalysed reactions]],<ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1021/ja01104a045| title= The Relationship between Michaelis Constants, Maximum Velocities and the Equilibrium Constant for an Enzyme-catalyzed Reaction| year= 1953| last1= Alberty| first1= Robert A.| journal= Journal of the American Chemical Society| volume= 75| issue= 8| pages= 1928–1932| bibcode= 1953JAChS..75.1928A}}</ref><ref name="fumarase1">{{cite journal | doi= 10.1021/ja01104a043| title= Studies of the Enzyme Fumarase. I. Kinetics and Equilibrium| year= 1953| last1= Bock| first1= Robert M.| last2= Alberty| first2= Robert A.| journal= Journal of the American Chemical Society| volume= 75| issue= 8| pages= 1921–1925| bibcode= 1953JAChS..75.1921B}}</ref> initially studying [[fumarase]] in particular.<ref name="fumarase1"/> He was among the first to consider the kinetics of reactions with more than one substrate,<ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1021/ja01541a001| title= On the Determination of Rate Constants for Coenzyme Mechanisms1| year= 1958| last1= Alberty| first1= Robert A.| journal= Journal of the American Chemical Society| volume= 80| issue= 8| pages= 1777–1782| bibcode= 1958JAChS..80.1777A}}</ref> and in the years that followed there was hardly any aspect of enzyme kinetics he did not touch, his work including, for example, studies of pH,<ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1016/0006-3002(54)90340-6| title= On the interpretation of the pH variation of the maximum initial velocity of an enzyme-catalyzed reaction| year= 1954| last1= Alberty| first1= Robert A.| last2= Massey| first2= Vincent| journal= Biochimica et Biophysica Acta| volume= 13| issue= 3| pages= 347–353| pmid= 13140346}}</ref> integrated rate equations,<ref name= "inte">{{cite journal | doi= 10.1021/ja01581a011| title= Studies of the Enzyme Fumarase. VII.1 Series Solutions of Integrated Rate Equations for Irreversible and Reversible Michaelis-Menten Mechanisms2| year= 1957| last1= Alberty| first1= Robert A.| last2= Koerber| first2= Barbara M.| journal= Journal of the American Chemical Society| volume= 79| issue= 24| pages= 6379–6382| bibcode= 1957JAChS..79.6379A}}</ref> reversible reactions,<ref name = "inte"/> effects of temperature,<ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1021/ja00898a003| title= The Temperature Dependence of the Steady State Kinetic Parameters of the Fumarase Reaction| year= 1963| last1= Brant| first1= David A.| last2= Barnett| first2= Lewis B.| last3= Alberty| first3= Robert A.| journal= Journal of the American Chemical Society| volume= 85| issue= 15| pages= 2204–2209| bibcode= 1963JAChS..85.2204B}}</ref> effects of buffers and inhibitors,<ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1073/pnas.39.9.895| title= Alteration of the Kinetic Properties of an Enzyme by the Binding of Buffer, Inhibitor, or Substrate| year= 1953| last1= Alberty| first1= R. A.| last2= Bock| first2= R. M.| journal= Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences| volume= 39| issue= 9| pages= 895–900| pmid= 16589350| pmc= 1063877| bibcode= 1953PNAS...39..895A| doi-access= free}}</ref> and others.

Alberty's early interest in the ionization of adenosine phosphates<ref>{{cite journal| title = The apparent ionization constants of the adenosine phosphates and related compounds
 | last1 = Alberty  | first1 = R A 
  | last2 = smith  |  first2 = R M
 | last3 = Bock  | first3 = R M
 | journal = J. Biol. Chem.
 | volume =  193  | issue= 1  | pages = 425–434
 | date = 1951| doi = 10.1016/S0021-9258(19)52468-1 | pmid = 14907730 | doi-access = free}}</ref>
and of thermodynamic aspects of biochemical reactions<ref>{{cite journal
 | title = Standard Gibbs free energy, enthalpy, and entropy changes as a function of pH and pMg for several reactions involving adenosine phosphates
 | last1 = Alberty  | first1 = R A 
 | journal = J. Biol. Chem.
 | volume =  244  | issue= 12  | pages = 3290–3302
 | date = 1969| doi = 10.1016/S0021-9258(18)93127-3 | pmid = 4307313 | doi-access = free}}</ref> came to be his primary interest, and in his later years he had numerous publications on this topic, such as a compilation of the properties of [[Adenosine triphosphate|ATP]] and related compounds.<ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1021/bi00158a025| title= Standard thermodynamic formation properties for the adenosine 5'-triphosphate series| year= 1992| last1= Alberty| first1= Robert A.| last2= Goldberg| first2= Robert N.| journal= Biochemistry| volume= 31| issue= 43| pages= 10610–10615| pmid= 1420176}}</ref> He worked with [[IUPAC]] on recommendations for presenting data for biochemical thermodynamics.<ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1016/j.bpc.2011.03.007| title= Recommendations for terminology and databases for biochemical thermodynamics| year= 2011| last1= Alberty| first1= Robert A.| last2= Cornish-Bowden| first2= Athel| last3= Goldberg| first3= Robert N.| last4= Hammes| first4= Gordon G.| last5= Tipton| first5= Keith| last6= Westerhoff| first6= Hans V.| journal= Biophysical Chemistry| volume= 155| issue= 2–3| pages= 89–103| pmid= 21501921}}</ref>

Although he was primarily concerned with single enzyme-catalysed reactions, Alberty also did some work with systems of more than one enzyme, such as the urea cycle.<ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1016/S0006-3495(97)78879-9| title= Constraints and missing reactions in the urea cycle| year= 1997| last1= Alberty| first1= R.A.| journal= Biophysical Journal| volume= 72| issue= 5| pages= 2349–2356| pmid= 9129838| pmc= 1184430| bibcode= 1997BpJ....72.2349A}}</ref>
